This guide uses the [GitHub development build](https://github.com/xec-cm/biocroxytest/tree/devel).
Set up the unified roclet and your test suites as described in
[Introduction to biocroxytest](biocroxytest.html). The named-case runners
require testthat 3.3.0 or newer.

## Share assertions across suites

In an `@testCases` tag, give the group a name and provide a literal list
of named cases and a shared `test` block. Each case chooses a suite and can
provide setup code. The setup and test run together in the same testthat
environment, once per case.

```{r named-declaration, eval=FALSE}
#' Increment an integer vector
#'
#' @param x An integer vector.
#' @return An integer vector.
#' @export
#' @testCases arithmetic
#' list(
#'   cases = list(
#'     small = list(suite = "tests", setup = { x <- 2L }),
#'     large = list(suite = "longtests", setup = { x <- seq_len(10000L) })
#'   ),
#'   test = { expect_identical(increment(x), x + 1L) }
#' )
increment <- function(x) x + 1L
```

Each ID combines the group and case names, so `arithmetic/large` keeps
its ID if the declaration moves to another source file or suite. The
planner reads declarations without loading the consumer package.

```{r plan-and-run, eval=FALSE}
before <- biocroxytest::test_case_plan()
roxygen2::roxygenise()
biocroxytest::run_test_case("arithmetic/large")

# After editing the declarations
biocroxytest::compare_test_plans(before, biocroxytest::test_case_plan())
```

The comparison reports additions, removals, suite moves and changes to
test code or fixtures. Use the full suite to exercise custom runners or
dependencies between cases.

## Pin fixture files

Add `fs` to the consumer package's `Suggests` and declare fixtures in
the case's `fixtures` list. For a local file, use a path relative to the
case's suite directory and obtain its checksum with `tools::md5sum()`.
For example, put `counts.tsv` in `tests/testthat/`, then use this entry in
the named `cases` list.

```r
table = list(
  suite = "tests",
  fixtures = list(
    counts = list(source = "counts.tsv", md5 = "<32-digit checksum>")
  )
)
```

Read the verified file in the setup or test using
`fixture_paths[["counts"]]`. A required fixture with missing or different
bytes blocks execution in the named runner. Set `required = FALSE` to
handle unavailability as an `NA_character_` path.

For an HTTPS source, install BiocFileCache and run
`biocroxytest::run_test_plan(download_fixtures = TRUE)` to allow downloads.
Later runs can reuse the verified cache offline. Standard testthat runs
check local fixtures and skip cases that require a remote fixture.
Keep generated or temporary data setup in the case, with cleanup for
files such as HDF5 backing stores.

### Share a file between suites

Keep a small shared fixture under `inst/extdata` in the consumer package
and add `fs` to its `Suggests`. Use `fs::path_package()` inside the test to
find the same file in a source package loaded for development or in an
installed package. The first argument is the consumer package name.
The installed path starts at `extdata`, so omit `inst` from the call.

```{r shared-fixture, eval=FALSE}
file <- fs::path_package("mypackage", "extdata", "expected.txt")
expect_identical(unname(tools::md5sum(file)), "8c213d966298ecd26ef240b3703d46e9")
expect_identical(scan(file, what = integer(), quiet = TRUE), c(3L, 6L))
```

This checksum corresponds to a file with `3` and `6` on separate lines,
each ending in LF. Compute the checksum from your own fixture. Both
suites can use the same path and assertions. Files retained from the
consumer's `inst` directory contribute to the revision fingerprint.
The checksum check above is a test assertion. The `fixtures` field of
the report describes files declared in `fixtures`, such as in the
suite-relative example above.

## Record what ran

```{r execution-evidence, eval=FALSE}
evidence <- biocroxytest::run_test_plan(ids = "arithmetic/large", seed = 42L)
evidence$cases
evidence$fixtures
```

Each case runs in a fresh R session and temporary package copy. The
report records the source fingerprint, elapsed time, fixture checks and
R environment. A `completed` case reached the end with a passing
assertion and no skips. The other states are `failed`, `skipped`,
`incomplete` and `missing`. For example, stale generated code or a
skip after a passing assertion is incomplete.

The copy and its revision fingerprint use the same input manifest. It
includes `DESCRIPTION`, `NAMESPACE`, `.BBSoptions`, `.Rbuildignore`,
`.Rinstignore`, license and build scripts, and the standard package
directories `R`, `src`, `data`, `inst`, `man`, `vignettes`, `demo`, `po`,
`tools` and `exec`. Build ignore patterns are matched without regard to
case. Standard editor and native build artifacts are skipped in the usual
package directories. Both test suites are retained in full, including helpers
and local fixtures used only during development. Roxygen templates in
`man-roxygen` and tooling in `man/roxygen` are also retained. Git metadata
is excluded.

If a test or roclet uses inputs outside those paths, declare each extra
file or directory on its own line in the source package's `DESCRIPTION`.
For example, this includes an example script and a directory of reference
data that would otherwise be omitted.

```text
Config/biocroxytest/inputs: dev/example-code.R
    reference-data
```

Use existing paths relative to the package root. Retained paths must be
ordinary files or directories. A declaration can retain build-excluded
development inputs, while excluded R sources stay excluded. Remove newly
excluded files from any `Collate` fields before checking generated tests
or installing the package. Direct calls to `roxygen2::roxygenise()` use
roxygen2's configured loader, which can load ignored R files before the
test roclet selects its sources. Older replay records continue to use
the original source selection and full-checkout fingerprint.

Set `timeout` in seconds to limit each isolated R process. A timeout
leaves the case incomplete and the plan continues. The limit includes
package loading and suite hooks. Fixture preparation happens first.

## Require cases in CI

Pass the required IDs explicitly so a missing case fails the check.

```{r require-cases, eval=FALSE}
required <- c("arithmetic/small", "arithmetic/large")
evidence <- biocroxytest::run_test_plan(ids = required, timeout = 60)
biocroxytest::check_test_plan(evidence, required)
```

An uncaught error from either call gives a nonzero exit status in
`Rscript`. The check requires `completed` and zero recorded warnings for
each required case. Use `allow_warnings = TRUE` to accept recorded warnings
for completed cases. Reports created before warning counts were recorded
need a fresh run to satisfy the default policy.

In a temporary copy of [dar at `27c4da2`](https://github.com/MicrobialGenomics-IrsicaixaOrg/dar/blob/27c4da2/tests/testthat/test-model-adapters.R),
we ran its DESeq2 contrast test as a named case. The assertions passed
with DESeq2 installed. A deliberate skip to simulate an unavailable
dependency produced a skipped result in testthat and failed the explicit
required-case policy. This is useful for CI jobs where a particular
dependency must be exercised.

## Compare runs across environments

Save a report from each CI job or R session. Use the same source,
fixtures, seed and IDs for a comparison across R versions or platforms.
For different backends, include their case IDs in the expected list.

```{r save-case-report, eval=FALSE}
ids <- c("arithmetic/small", "arithmetic/large")
report <- biocroxytest::run_test_plan(ids = ids, seed = 42L)
saveRDS(report, "../test-evidence.rds")
```

Retrieve the reports as `left-evidence.rds` and `right-evidence.rds`
and match the expected IDs to each report.
Here `NA` means an expected ID has no row in the report. A status of
`missing` means the runner did have a row for the case and found its
generated test or result missing. Choose the expected IDs independently
of the reports so the table also shows IDs absent from both runs.
Older reports without warning counts show `NA` in that column.

```{r compare-case-reports, eval=FALSE}
left <- readRDS("left-evidence.rds")
right <- readRDS("right-evidence.rds")
expected <- c("arithmetic/small", "arithmetic/large")

summarize_run <- function(report) {
  cases <- report$cases[match(expected, report$cases$id), ]
  warnings <- cases$warnings
  if (is.null(warnings)) warnings <- rep(NA_integer_, length(expected))
  context <- function(field) {
    vapply(expected, function(id) {
      value <- report$environments[[id]][[field]]
      if (is.null(value)) NA_character_ else value
    }, character(1))
  }
  data.frame(
    id = expected, status = cases$status, warnings = warnings,
    r_version = context("r_version"), platform = context("platform")
  )
}

comparison <- merge(summarize_run(left), summarize_run(right),
                    by = "id", suffixes = c(".left", ".right"), all = TRUE)
comparison
c(left = left$revision, right = right$revision)
```

Check the revision hashes before interpreting the differences.
For a particular ID, look in `report$environments[[id]]$packages` for
loaded package versions and in `report$fixtures[[id]]` for declared
fixture checks. A dependency version describes the run environment.
Use an assertion on the backing class in a backend-specific test to
confirm which implementation ran.

## Replay a failed case

The [sample-alignment walkthrough](replay-walkthrough.html) runs a failing
case, reproduces the failure from a replay record and checks the fix.

If the case is `failed`, save its record outside the package tree so it
does not change the source fingerprint.

```{r replay-failure, eval=FALSE}
record <- biocroxytest::write_test_replay(
  evidence, "arithmetic/large", "../arithmetic-failure.rds"
)
record$command
replayed <- biocroxytest::replay_test_case("../arithmetic-failure.rds")
replayed$comparison
```

Replay checks the package revision and fixture identities, restores the
base R seed and reports whether failure messages and available source
locations matched. It also reports changes to the recorded environment.
Use the same package source and fixtures, and set backend-specific seeds
in the case setup when needed.

## Reduce a paired failure

For a paired SummarizedExperiment with two conditions and one sample per
condition per pair, `biocroxytest::reduce_paired_failure()` can find a
smaller regression fixture. Supply the pair and condition columns, an
additive design and a checker that returns a stable identifier for the
target failure or `NULL` when it is absent.

```{r reduce-paired, eval=FALSE}
reduced <- biocroxytest::reduce_paired_failure(
  x, pair = "subject", condition = "visit", design = ~ subject + visit,
  check = check_known_failure
)
dim(reduced$data)
reduced$failure
```

The reducer removes rows and whole pairs, keeps a full-rank design with
positive residual degrees of freedom, and checks the final subset again.
Review it before writing an ordinary test of the expected correct
behavior. An HDF5-backed subset still uses its backing file.
